overview: Set on about eleven acres in Hoskote, this community is planned around a simple idea: give families generous homes, then surround them with open space. Roughly 81 percent of the site is kept open, organised along a central landscaped spine that links the amphitheatre, play areas and sports courts, so the walk from the gate to your door passes through greenery rather than parking.

The 3 BHK residences come in two layouts of 1,735 and 1,945 square feet of super built-up area, with a carpet-area efficiency the developer puts at about 70 percent including balconies. Terrace balconies of roughly 13 by 10 feet extend the living room outdoors, and the plans separate the living zone from bedrooms so that daily life and quiet time can coexist.

A corten-steel clad clubhouse of about 62,000 square feet, including under-tower amenities, anchors the social life of the community with a temperature-controlled pool, co-working space, age-designated play areas and a dozen sporting facilities. Around 22,500 square feet of retail is planned at the entrance for everyday convenience.

Hoskote sits along the highway on Bengaluru's eastern edge, with the developer highlighting direct access toward the airport and the Whitefield employment belt. Sustainability measures published for the project include rainwater harvesting, an organic waste converter, solar power and a higher green cover for a cooler microclimate.

overview: Mizumi Reserve is conceived as a self-contained township off HSR Layout, nestled between two lakes in the Harlur Road and Kudlu belt of South Bengaluru. The developer describes about 80 acres for the full township, with roughly 77 percent kept as open space, so that homes look out over water, tree-lined boulevards and sports lawns rather than at each other.

The current phase offers 3 and 4 BHK homes, with the 3 BHK layouts at 1,901 and 2,165 square feet of super built-up area and living balconies of up to 170 square feet that act as an extra room for most of the year. A distinctive grey-brick façade gives the towers a calm, tactile character that ages well in Bengaluru's climate.

Each phase is planned with its own clubhouse of more than 63,000 square feet, and the community lists over thirty indoor and outdoor amenities: a swimming pool, gymnasium, yoga and meditation zones, co-working lounges, tennis, padel and pickleball courts, box cricket, a farmers' market zone and an amphitheatre.

The location puts residents within the developer's stated short drives of schools, hospitals, Sarjapur Road and the Outer Ring Road technology corridor. Published sustainability features include rainwater capture, solar power, an organic waste converter and a higher green cover across the site.

overview: Muse & Maison is a single tower of 128 homes on about two acres in Gattahalli, off Hosa Road. It is deliberately small. Where larger townships trade on scale, this address trades on intimacy: one lobby, one community, and 78 percent of the site given over to gardens, a pool and courtyards.

The architecture is defined by a terracotta skin of jaali screens that filters light into the lobbies, yoga deck and corridors, giving the building a warm, handmade texture. Inside, the 3 BHK residences come as corner units of 1,930 square feet and middle units of 1,877 square feet of super built-up area, with luxury terrace balconies of up to 12 by 8 feet.

A clubhouse of about 13,000 square feet is sized for the people who live here rather than for show: a temperature-controlled pool, gymnasium, steam rooms, library, multipurpose hall, board-games room and co-working space, with padel and pickleball courts, a sports pavilion and age-specific play areas in the grounds.

Hosa Road connects the community to Electronic City, HSR Layout and the Sarjapur technology belt, and the developer notes the Hosa Road metro station nearby. Published sustainability measures include rainwater harvesting, solar power, an organic waste converter and increased green cover.

overview: Trees & Tandem takes its name seriously. On seven acres off Sarjapur Road, the developer has retained more than a hundred existing trees and kept about 90 percent of the site open, so the towers rise out of a mature landscape rather than a cleared one. Tower lobbies mirror each other across a wide central garden, and a tree-lined boulevard runs from the gate to the clubhouse.

Only 364 homes share the site, all 3 BHK, in two layouts of 1,885 and 2,142 square feet of super built-up area with a floor-plan efficiency the developer puts at about 76 percent. Large living balconies, tucked-in wardrobes and generous bedrooms are the recurring themes, with contemporary brick-finish exteriors that sit comfortably among the trees.

The Club, a clubhouse of 16,400 square feet, hosts a temperature-controlled pool, gym, steam room, yoga room, games room, billiards and co-working, while the grounds carry fifteen-plus sports amenities including tennis, badminton, padel, pickleball, box cricket and a skating rink, with a sculpture park, amphitheatre and farmers' market for weekends.

The address sits near RGA Tech Park and Electronic City Phase 2 and the developer highlights metro access on the Yellow Line. Published sustainability measures, branded Carbon Healing Homes, include rainwater capture, zero waste to landfill with on-site composting, solar power informed by sun-path analysis, and a cooler microclimate from retained green cover.

Ground-floor Garden units open onto private-use gardens of roughly 1,900 square feet, while Open Terrace units above trade the lawn for a sky terrace. Luxury terrace balconies, double-height arrival gates and a courtyard pool give the community the proportions of a villa estate without the upkeep of one.

A grand clubhouse of about 18,000 square feet holds the temperature-controlled pool, indoor gym, yoga room, steam and change rooms, party hall, billiards and indoor games, with tennis, padel, pickleball, net cricket, an outdoor gym, maze garden, amphitheatre and party lawn across the grounds, for more than 25 amenities in all.

Hennur Main Road places the community within the developer's stated drives of Manyata Tech Park, the Outer Ring Road and Kempegowda International Airport.
